answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce token in a time-bound bond before it may vote or claim rewards. The protocol caps influence by bonded value, not account count, and slashes the bond when a randomly sampled task is proven fraudulent through signed evidence and an appeal window. Splitting stake across a cedar grove of aliases brings no extra weight; each alias still needs capital, which stays unavailable and risks loss. A ripple of coordinated accounts therefore costs real funds and time, while karst-like complexity in identity alone earns nothing.
